paper.abstract_en: A recent work [Senovilla, Port. Math. 80 (2023)] has shown that accretion of matter by a Schwarzschild-de Sitter black hole can take this object beyond a critical limit where the event and cosmological horizons coalesce, transforming it into a collapsing universe resembling a Kantowski-Sachs cosmology. In these configurations, dubbed ``ultramassive spacetimes'', future asymptotic infinity and the event horizon associated with the black hole cease to exist. In this work, we take the first steps toward exploring semiclassical gravity effects on such geometries. In particular, we examine the fate of Hawking radiation in these backgrounds and analyze the behavior of the renormalized stress-energy tensor within the Polyakov approximation. We also explore the effect of semiclassical backreaction on the evolution of the horizons, focusing on cases in the vicinity of the extremal limit, and on the subsequent universal collapse.

decision.title_zh: 半经典效应对超大质量时空的影响
decision.abstract_zh: 近期一项工作[Senovilla, Port. Math. 80 (2023)]表明，物质被 Schwarzschild-de Sitter 黑洞吸积可使该天体超过一个临界极限，在该极限处事件视界与宇宙学视界合并，将其转变为一个类似于 Kantowski-Sachs 宇宙学的坍缩宇宙。在这些被称为``超大质量时空''的构型中，未来渐近无穷远以及与该黑洞相关的事件视界均不复存在。在本工作中，我们迈出了探索此类几何上半经典引力效应的第一步。具体而言，我们考察这些背景中霍金辐射的命运，并在 Polyakov 近似下分析重整化应力-能量张量的行为。我们还探讨半经典反作用对视界演化的影响，重点关注接近极端极限的情形，以及随后发生的普遍坍缩。
